text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. By analyzing these examples, they learn patterns in language, allowing them to predict the next word in a sentence. When you write a prompt, the model uses this knowledge to generate a response that sounds human. Prompt engineering is the skill of carefully wording your request to get the best answer. LLMs can write emails, summarize information, and even code. However, they have limits. They don't truly understand meaning and can produce false or biased facts. Also, their knowledge stops at a certain date, so they can't know the newest events unless given that data.
